payload.statement: Of 135 in-frame STAT3 variants reported in AD-HIES, only six had been experimentally shown to be dominant negative; the authors experimentally tested 143 variants.
4 of 6 experimental structures of P40763 in the Protein Data Bank observe residue 382.
PDB entry 6NJS (X-RAY DIFFRACTION, 2.7 Å, deposited 2019-01-04) observes residue 382 of P40763: Stat3 Core in complex with compound SD36; ligands KQV.

The partial loss-of-function STAT3 variant p.Arg417Thr (a different DNA-binding-region residue, not R382W) maintained normal DNA binding but showed reduced IL-6-induced transcriptional activity and no negative dominance.
PDB entry 6QHD (X-RAY DIFFRACTION, 2.85 Å, deposited 2019-01-16) observes residue 382 of P40763: Lysine acetylated and tyrosine phosphorylated STAT3 in a complex with DNA; no non-solvent ligand.
A heterozygous STAT3 nonsense mutation led to rapid decay of the mutant mRNA and protein, causing haploinsufficiency; Stat3+/- mice had increased IgE and reduced TH17 differentiation.
PDB entry 6TLC (X-RAY DIFFRACTION, 2.9 Å, deposited 2019-12-02) observes residue 382 of P40763: Unphosphorylated human STAT3 in complex with MS3-6 monobody; no non-solvent ligand.

The STAT3 variant p.K709N (a different residue, not R382W) is reported to cause hyper-IgE syndrome likely by impaired STAT3-dimer formation (per the article title; the retrieved abstract was truncated before its results).
PDB entry 6NUQ (X-RAY DIFFRACTION, 3.15 Å, deposited 2019-02-01) observes residue 382 of P40763: Stat3 Core in complex with compound SI109; ligands KQV.
Autosomal dominant hyper-IgE syndrome is described as caused by heterozygous loss-of-function STAT3 mutations with a dominant-negative effect, the prototype of these disorders.
AlphaFold DB model AF-P40763-F1 covers the full sequence of P40763 (mean pLDDT 84.88).
ClinVar lists NM_139276.3(STAT3):c.1145G>A (p.Arg382Gln) at the same residue as Pathogenic (criteria provided, multiple submitters, no conflicts).

No retrieved paper tests STAT3 p.Arg382Trp itself for DNA binding, dimerization, phosphorylation, or dominant-negative activity; the functional data found are for other residues (Arg417Thr, Lys709Asn) or for a nonsense variant.
payload.why_it_matters: Without a functional assay on R382W, it cannot be decided whether this substitution acts by dominant negativity, haploinsufficiency, or partial loss of function.

payload.statement: R382 in the DNA-binding domain contacts the DNA phosphate backbone, and Arg-to-Trp removes that positive charge and adds a bulky hydrophobic side chain, so STAT3 binds its response element less well.
payload.would_refute: The R382 side chain in DNA-bound structures (for example 6QHD) lies more than about 5 Å from every DNA atom, and its substitution in a model of the DNA complex creates no steric or electrostatic clash with the DNA.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: Only the direct evidence about this substitution points here: UniProt E2 reports reduced DNA-binding ability for R382W, and E3 places residue 382 in the STAT DNA-binding domain. E12 is a DNA-complex structure that observes residue 382. Missing: no structure shows R382 contacting DNA directly (G2), and no assay tests R382W binding (G1).

payload.statement: R382 packs into or stabilises the DNA-binding domain fold, and the bulky Trp side chain destabilises the domain so that less folded, functional STAT3 is available.
payload.would_refute: Predicted ΔΔG for R382W (for example with FoldX or Rosetta on the AlphaFold model and on 6QHD) is near zero or stabilising, and R382 side-chain burial is low in all experimental structures, so no packing defect is predicted.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: Conservation (E5), popEVE (E6), EVE (E7) and AlphaMissense (E4) all predict damage, but these tools score deleteriousness and do not separate fold destabilisation from loss of DNA contact. The record has no stability measurement and no protein-level data for R382W (G4), and the only haploinsufficiency evidence (E13) concerns a nonsense variant. So this ranks below the binding-specific hypothesis.

payload.statement: R382 sits at a STAT3 homodimer contact in the DNA-binding domain, and R382W disrupts dimer formation, which is needed for stable DNA binding and gives a dominant-negative effect through inactive heterodimers with wild-type STAT3.
payload.would_refute: In homodimeric STAT3 structures and in a docked or predicted dimer model, no atom of R382 lies within about 5 Å of the partner chain, and R382W leaves the predicted interface energy and the dimer geometry unchanged.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: The dominant-negative framing of AD-HIES (E17, E8) is general to the disease and not specific to this residue. E15 concerns a different residue (K709N), so it is indirect support only. Nothing in the record maps R382 to an interface (G6 notes interface residues are unmapped). It ranks last because it has the least direct support.

payload.summary: Three agent-generated hypotheses are recorded for STAT3 p.Arg382Trp loss of function. H1 (nucleic_acid_binding, rank 1) is favoured because UniProt reports reduced DNA binding for this exact substitution and residue 382 sits in the DNA-binding domain. H2 (stability_folding, rank 2) and H3 (protein_interaction, rank 3) are competing mechanisms. All three can be tested computationally: check R382 contacts in 6QHD and other DNA-bound structures, run ΔΔG on the AlphaFold model, and check dimer interface contacts. Gaps G1, G2 and G5 should be closed first.

PLAN: choose ONE targeted computational test within the remaining budget (160 tool calls, 300 compute seconds) that discriminates H1 (DNA-binding, currently favoured), H2 (stability/folding) and H3 (dimer interface). Use the refutation criteria in H1-H3. Subject line: variant_id=STAT3-p.Arg382Trp gene=STAT3 accession=P40763 position=382 reference=R alternate=W.

payload.description: FoldX predicted folding free-energy change for R382W on the AlphaFold model via EBI ProtVar, with pLDDT at the residue and the other disease substitutions at position 382. Tests H2 directly: a destabilising value (at or above the threshold) supports H2; a neutral or stabilising value weakens it, which is H2's refutation criterion.
payload.expected_learning_reasoning: H2 is ranked 2 and this is the only test that measures its refutation criterion. A destabilising result would move H2 up to contest H1 as favourite. A neutral or stabilising result would drop H2 and leave H1 and H3 as the live options. It does not separate H1 from H3, so the gain is capped at about half.

controls: Within-site comparison: the same predictor for the other substitutions reported at this residue.
Applicability control: the model confidence (pLDDT) at the residue, because FoldX on a low-confidence region is not interpretable.

payload.description: P2Rank and ProtVar on the AlphaFold model: whether R382 lines a predicted pocket (rank and probability) and whether it lies in a predicted protein-protein interface. Tests H3 (interface membership) and weakly H1 and H2 through the pocket result.
payload.expected_learning_reasoning: ProtVar already reports interface state None for this residue, so the likely outcome is no predicted interface. That would weaken H3 but does not refute it, since H3's criterion needs homodimer structures or a docked model, which this test does not run. The pocket result bears on ligand binding, which none of H1 to H3 is about, so it cannot move H1. Expected movement is small.
payload.feasibility_reasoning: list_available_tests reports can_run true: ProtVar pocket and interface data answer for this residue, and P2Rank runs on the AlphaFold model. Cost is 0 compute seconds and 2 tool calls.
controls: Rank control: the rank and probability of the pocket among all predicted pockets of the model.
Confidence control: mean pLDDT of the pocket residues.
